source: docs/reports/w47-callee-closure-r2/README.md section 6, the eight classes; every name below was placed by reading its body or prototype (this card's report, section 5). Class 6 is the ranking's class (v), matched by builtin prefix in closure_r3.py.

2-in-place-lifecycles-and-reallocation.vocabulary: an out-slot or in-place lifecycle mode, and an in-place reallocation through T ** or of a field

4-handle-kinds-and-no-return.vocabulary: a handle kind (dlopen, the arena constructor, a constructor or destructor whose release is its own destructor) and a no-return effect

5-system-libraries-outside-the-audited-s.vocabulary: user decision 2026-09-28: quirin-audit plugin crates (W48-OPENSSL-CONTRACT-PLUGIN, W48-LIBCURL-CONTRACT-PLUGIN), out of scope here

6-compiler-builtins-without-an-owning-cr.vocabulary: an owner for compiler builtins (no provider crate owns them); the ranking's class (v)

7-monkey-backend-selected-static-inline-.vocabulary: a reading of the backend-selected static inline bodies included into mk_event.c

8-arena-interior-reading.vocabulary: W47-ARENA-INTERIOR-READING, accepted by the user as interim for the arena; the pool mode is W47-ARENA-POOL-RESULT-MODE. Extending the interior reading to a child the base allocates lazily and keeps in a field (rd_kafka_topic_partition_get_private) is the same decision

reader-gap-transparent-union.why: glibc's __SOCKADDR_ARG / __CONST_SOCKADDR_ARG transparent union, which the declared-ABI reader does not read (libc/socket.qv); a reader gap, not a vocabulary decision

no-owning-crate.why: xxHash's XXH_INLINE_ALL header bodies have no provider crate; creating one is an ownership decision, the builtin rule applied to a vendored library
